prompt_en: A photographic study of garment fit centers on a photographed woman wearing clothing with visible fit. She pauses between practical tasks. The supplied reference guides her visible face and hair: a short dark brown bob, airy fringe separating into fine strands, dark rounded eyes and a softly tapered face with natural rose lips. Her quiet, attentive presence and a small amused half-smile make the portrait feel personal. She stands in a working letterpress shop at violet dusk, just before the first print exhibition. A newly pulled cream proof sheet with still-damp charcoal ink hangs from two wooden clips on a short improvised drying cord behind her, stretching from a type cabinet to a metal post. The open stack of similar blank sheets and inked press rollers explain what has just happened. She has solved the drying-space problem with this awkward little line and now waits, looking toward the hanging sheet with private amusement. Her right hand holds one spare wooden clip at upper chest height, elbow close to her torso; her left arm falls naturally beside her hip, with the hand relaxed and visible. Her shoulders are level and both feet rest fully on the worn wooden floor, the right foot a small step forward. She wears a short charcoal brushed-wool single-breasted tailored jacket over an ivory ribbed knit and matching long straight trousers. The jacket shoulder seam meets the outer shoulder point, its sleeve hanging in a smooth vertical line to the wrist. A narrow roped ridge crowns each sleeve head just above that same jacket's shoulder attachment seam; a thin grazing highlight makes the two connected wool boundaries visible. Its fronts meet at one fastened button near the hem while the lower body of the jacket has generous space around her torso; the wool forms shallow vertical folds instead of taut diagonals at that button. The jacket hem ends just above the trouser waistband, leaving the waistband visible across the front. The trouser waistband follows her natural waist closely, then the fabric hangs freely through the thighs and knees. Each straight trouser leg reaches the top of a dark leather loafer with one soft fold above the instep, and the rear hem stays clear of the floor. The broad lapels, dry wool nap, pale ribbing and polished shoes produce distinct tactile rhythms; her body feels present inside the tailoring rather than disappearing into a garment silhouette. A dim amber task lamp warms her left cheek and the jacket edge, while the high window gives the workshop its cool violet depth. The high window grazes her right jacket shoulder and sleeve ridge with cool light, while the amber task lamp keeps its warm pool on her left cheek and the spare wooden clip. The coat and waist remain readable against a light plaster wall; the old press, type drawers, cord and cream paper stay softer and subordinate. Use a vertical portrait frame with breathing room above her hair and beneath the soles. Photograph her full length from head to both soles in a three-quarter frontal view, the camera at lower-chest height and several steps away. Keep her entire jacket, waistband, both trouser legs and shoes plainly visible, with the press set behind and to the side. The modest perspective, calm eye line and material detail create an intimate environmental fashion photograph whose meaning comes from the practical waiting moment.
